name: Hakeem Jeffries
role: U.S. representative from New York (2013-present); House Democratic Leader (2023-present)
summary: Mainstream liberal Democrat who frames his politics as a Black progressive tradition rather than democratic socialism. He supports abortion rights, marriage equality, gun-safety laws, criminal justice reform, labor rights, public health insurance programs and climate investment, and opposes open borders, defunding the police and abolishing the Senate. He is strongly pro-Israel while now calling for a Palestinian state and a change in Israel policy, backs NATO and Ukraine, and opposes Trump's tariffs, ICE tactics and the Iran war.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Says high-quality, affordable healthcare should be a right for every American and defends and expands the ACA, Medicare and Medicaid; he cosponsored Medicare for All from 2013 to 2021 but said in August 2026 he does not currently support it, so the evidence is mixed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sponsored the House bill to raise the federal minimum wage to $15 (2019) and earlier backed $10.10; joined the push for a higher wage than $7.25.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Criticises the permanent tax breaks for billionaire donors and presents the Inflation Reduction Act as paid for by taxes on the largest corporations and ultra-wealthy; has not stated a specific higher rate.

unions-good.rationale: Introduced the PRO Act to protect the right to organize, calling it essential to better working conditions, and opposed stripping federal workers' collective bargaining rights.

cut-welfare.rationale: Condemns Republican cuts to SNAP and Medicaid ('weaponize hunger') and describes Social Security, Medicaid, nutrition aid and the ACA as the strong floor government should provide.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Said in 2026 that mass surveillance of American citizens is unacceptable and in 2013 asked to end bulk data collection, although his caucus supplied votes for a FISA reauthorisation in 2024.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Called for deschedule and decriminalization of marijuana (MORE Act) and an end to the war on drugs, but did not address all recreational drugs.

strong-leader.rationale: Argues Congress must act as a separate, coequal branch, says 'there are no kings', and opposed Trump's unilateral tariffs and war actions.

state-harmful.rationale: Describes government programs as the necessary strong floor for working people and campaigns to defend them.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports an assault-weapons ban and universal background checks, voted for the Protecting Our Kids Act (age 21 for semiautomatic rifles, magazine limits, safe storage, ghost guns) and opposes concealed carry.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mixed: opposes defunding police and cuts to law-enforcement grants, while pushing federal police reform and restraints on ICE.

rehabilitation.rationale: Says the US relies on mass incarceration rather than rehabilitation and led the FIRST STEP Act to expand counseling, education and job training for prisoners.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for and helped lead the Respect for Marriage Act, saying love does not discriminate and the law should not.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act, cosponsors it, and calls a woman's right to choose non-negotiable.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Cosponsors H.R. 40 to study reparations, saying systemic racism has been in the soil since 1619 and the country will not 'simply move on'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Backs comprehensive reform with a pathway to citizenship and backed larger family-based and high-skill visa caps.

open-borders.rationale: Said 'I certainly don't support open borders'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says Congress can no longer afford procrastination on climate, backed the Inflation Reduction Act as the largest climate investment, and condemns the repeal of the endangerment finding.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Backed raising the estate tax to its 1990s level (2015) to raise revenue.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Calls Trump's tariffs disastrous, wants them rolled back, and praised the Supreme Court ruling against them.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Voted for and promotes the CHIPS and Science Act, which gives $39 billion in federal incentives to build domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

democracy-best.rationale: Frames the US and Ukraine as standing for democracy against autocracy and says Democrats will always defend democracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Stated that violence is never the answer, whether targeted at the right, the left or the centre.

accelerate-technology.rationale: On AI, called for decisive action 'to slow down the pace of development' to protect Americans.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Criticised the push to acquire Greenland and the Venezuela operation as extreme foreign adventures.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Calls America's commitment to Israel's right to exist as a Jewish and democratic state and homeland for the Jewish people ironclad.

school-vouchers.rationale: Opposed private and religious school voucher programs (2015), although he has long supported public charter schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Supported the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan as stimulus and has long backed federal stimulus spending, while criticising Trump-era deficits.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backs an independent Palestinian state with self-determination alongside Israel and defends Ukraine's territorial integrity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted against maintaining a work requirement for welfare recipients in 2013 (House vote) and opposes the Medicaid cuts in the 2025 reconciliation law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Calls the filibuster and recent state tactics 'Jim Crow' relics and defends the 14th Amendment's equal protection promise.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Mixed: an early statement favoured more oil and gas with limits on greenhouse gases and he voted to ban offshore drilling in the Gulf; the Inflation Reduction Act he backs also boosts domestic energy production.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Demands independent investigations and state or local prosecution when ICE agents break the law, and backed the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backs a broad government role: Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, the ACA, housing and infrastructure investment.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Stresses the 14th Amendment's equal protection and 'liberty and justice for all' as American values.

separated-powers.rationale: Says the Framers made Congress separate and coequal and that Congress should act as a check on the executive.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Argues diversity is an American value ('E pluribus unum') and that attacking diversity, equity and inclusion attacks the United States.

party-controls-media.rationale: Called the arrest of journalists a disgraceful affront to the First Amendment and demanded Don Lemon be freed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Called withdrawing from NATO a reckless choice and says the US needs more friends, not adversaries.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Welcomed the Supreme Court ruling that all persons born in the US are citizens under the 14th Amendment.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports an independent Palestinian state and calls West Bank settlement expansion illegal under international law.

collective-defense.rationale: Says the US should not walk away from NATO, an alliance that kept the world safe, and calls Denmark a NATO ally.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Argues no one is above the law, saying 'there are no kings' and that the Fourth Amendment is not optional for ICE or the executive.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Supported affirmative action in 2008 and defends diversity, equity and inclusion programmes now; he has not addressed the 2023 admissions ruling in sources I opened.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted for the Equality Act and the Respect for Marriage Act and calls for banning discrimination by sexual orientation and gender identity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: As House impeachment manager argued President Trump should be removed for abuse of power, and voted to impeach him twice.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Led the House amendment to bar Confederate flag sales and display on National Park Service land and said the 'Ghosts of the Confederacy have invaded the GOP'.

corporate-influence.rationale: Wants dramatic campaign finance reform, earlier backed public financing by small-donor vouchers and full disclosure of campaign spending, and attacks corruption in the Trump administration.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Honors the six million Jewish lives lost in the Holocaust and calls its crimes uniquely horrific.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Supports marriage equality and the Equality Act's anti-discrimination protections.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemns the Trump administration for weaponizing the Justice Department against critics and journalists as an attack on the Constitution.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Voted for the Equality Act in 2019 and supports banning discrimination based on gender identity, though in 2016 he said gender identity should not be elevated as a protected class.

social-market-economy.rationale: Says the economy should have a 'strong floor and no ceiling' and that capitalism should serve the greatest number of people, with Social Security, Medicare and the ACA as the floor.

racial-franchise.rationale: Campaigns for the Voting Rights Act and against attacks on majority-Black districts as voter suppression.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Says he does not support defunding the police, backs police reform and law-enforcement grants, and seeks prison reform rather than abolition.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Argues government programs (Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, the ACA, nutrition aid) are the strong floor for working Americans.

term-limits.rationale: Said in 2008 he favours limits on campaign spending but not term limits.

abolish-ip.rationale: Calls the US intellectual property system vital to cultural and economic development and co-led the Music Modernization Act and the CASE Act.

second-chamber.rationale: Said he does not support abolishing the Senate.

free-public-college.rationale: Backed making two years of community college free (2015); no statement found on free tuition for all public colleges.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backs the PRO Act and objects to the executive order removing federal employees' collective bargaining rights; he has not addressed contract-versus-bargaining as such.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Promoted the American Rescue Plan's expansion of the Earned Income Tax Credit for low-wage workers and the larger Child Tax Credit.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Sponsored a bill to cancel college loans after ten years of repayment and his office promotes student loan forgiveness and debt relief programs.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Co-led the FIRST STEP Act, which reduced mandatory minimums, and backed the EQUAL Act, and argues sentences are often disproportionately long.

voter-id.rationale: Opposes the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship mandate as voter suppression and in 2014 opposed photo ID rules, while saying states may set their own ID rules.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says systemic racism remains in the soil of the country and identifies it as the defining problem for Black progressives, citing attacks on voting rights.

notes: Medicare for All: cosponsored 2013-2021, said in August 2026 he does not currently support it; the audit gives universal healthcare low confidence. Gender identity: 2016 remark against elevating it as a protected class is superseded by his 2019 Equality Act vote. Some older positions (2008-2015) come from the OnTheIssues index and may not reflect his current views.
